caveats.text: Contributions in the ban-window strip come from people name-matched to the principals (board members, officers, owners of more than 10%) listed on contractors' SFEC-126(f)4 filings, not from employer fields; a name match can still be wrong. Timing near a contract approval is a pattern worth checking, not proof of influence.

The "by source type" chart also counts people who named a contractor as their employer on Form 460; employees are not covered by the §1.126 ban unless they are also principals, so that bar is context, not a flag.

Candidates are labelled as candidates when the data show no evidence that they held City elective office (Board of Supervisors roster, Form 700 and lobbyist contact reports); an appointment the data do not capture would be missed.
